symptom: openptv-cloud e2e test fails intermittently (idle ~1 in 19, all cores busy ~1 in 2); only runs.wp4.trajectories.pos_sum moves, by ~0.04
bisect: sequence/correspondence output identical between a normal and a failing run (same 'Frame k had' lines)
tracker inputs at steps 1 and 2 bit-identical; the kernel call at step 2 adds 0 or 1 particle (trackcorr 'add')
mmlut tables and kernel settings identical; num_threads=1; PYTHONHASHSEED irrelevant; thread pool irrelevant
MallocScribble=1 (fill freed memory) flips step 2 from add 1 to add 0 -> the kernel reads recycled heap memory
libgmalloc MALLOC_PROTECT_BEFORE=1 + lldb: EXC_BAD_ACCESS in _trackcorr_particle_fast, a read just before an int32 array
root_causes: assess_new_position_fast_nogil writes tr_unused (-1) for a camera without a candidate; the consumers in track_kernels_corr tested '!= PT_UNUSED' (-999), so -1 passed and targ_tnr[ci, -1] was read and WRITTEN (-100). ci=0 touches the memory before the array; ci>0 touches the last (unused, -999) slot of the previous row.
candsearch_in_pix_fast* accepted any tnr != -1, so the temporary add-claim marker -100 was returned as a particle index and used as path_x_3[-100].
effect_of_old_code: an add with a camera missing was rejected because the unused slot holds -999 != -1; only for camera 0 the read hit heap garbage, which equalled -1 with some probability: a random extra added particle (wp4 frames 4 and 9)
fix: consumers test index >= 0 and an added particle requires a free blob in every camera (the effective old behaviour, now explicit); candidate search requires tnr >= 0

verification.cloud_e2e_10_runs_full_cpu_load: 10/10 pass without regenerating the reference (before: ~1/2 failed)

note: 30 tests of the pure-Python fallback (tests/unit/test_*_coverage.py, e.g. test_correspondences_coverage) fail on this machine with and without this change; 4 flowtracks-dependent tests fail in the compiled suite (not installed here).
